sections.html:
Henderson is a Clark County city about 16 miles southeast of Las Vegas, at roughly 1,867 feet of elevation and covering about 107 square miles. The July 1, 2025 population estimate is 353,289, second in Nevada behind Las Vegas. A Henderson seller shares a market, an airport and a school district with the bigger neighbor but deals with a different city hall.

Henderson incorporated on April 16, 1953. Most of its later growth took the form of master-planned communities: Green Valley first, then Anthem, Lake Las Vegas and Seven Hills. Many have homeowners associations, which is worth confirming for your own address before you list.

  • Green Valley, the first large master-planned neighborhood.
  • Anthem, Seven Hills and Lake Las Vegas, later communities with their own rules.
  • Older parts of the city, where you should check whether any association applies.

Summer heat is hardest on roofs, cooling equipment, paint and landscaping. If the air conditioner is old or the roof leaks, a buyer with a mortgage will likely ask for repairs, whereas a cash buyer may take the house unrepaired and lower the offer accordingly.

Valley storms can bring flash flooding. Homeowner's insurance leaves flood damage out, and the county directs owners to the National Flood Insurance Program. A regional flood control district created in 1986 handles drainage across the valley. Find out from your insurance agent if your parcel sits in a mapped flood zone, so you hear it before a buyer's lender does.

Henderson allows short-term vacation rentals only with annual city registration, and some developments are on a prohibited list where the city will not register a property. The city lists a non-refundable registration fee of $848, a certification class for the owner and the local contact, a Nevada business license in the owner's name, and a registered local contact who is either certified or a property manager under NRS 645. Registered properties must also file the room tax report and pay transient lodging tax monthly.

When the home sits in a common-interest community, the city's acknowledgement form requires that the rental be expressly authorized by the association.

A house that has hosted visitors should come with a clear statement of whether its registration is current. Do not assume the registration passes to a new owner without asking the city.

A 2021 Nevada law on nonfunctional turf leaves grass in single-family yards alone. Starting in 2027 it bars Colorado River water from member agencies on nonfunctional grass, and the water authority says it reaches commercial, multi-family, government and other properties.

Living in a condominium, or in an association with shared lawns? Then the deadline lands on the association, and a special assessment could show up in its budget. Buyers will ask. Get the association's most recent statement before listing.

NRS 113.130 requires Henderson sellers to complete Nevada's Seller's Real Property Disclosure Form. A buyer who closes with no completed form, or with no word of a known defect, can claim treble damages unless that right was waived.

The Clark County rate runs $2.55 per $500 of value: $1.95 from the state and $0.60 from the county. A declaration of value goes to the county recorder with the deed. NRS 375 lets either side be charged, so look at your contract to see who pays.

Henderson parcels are billed by Clark County. The full amount falls due the third Monday in August, or in installments for parcels over $100, with later ones on the first Mondays of October, January and March. NRS 361.483 puts a 4 percent penalty on a late installment and raises it as more are missed.

Anyone disputing an assessed value has until January 15 of the fiscal year to petition the County Board of Equalization, with a weekend or holiday pushing the date to the next business day.

NRS 361.4723 holds a primary residence to about a 3 percent annual rise in its tax bill. Because the statute treats a home rented to anyone beyond the owner and family as something else, a former rental may miss out.

sections.h2: If you owe tax or HOA dues
sections.html:
Both open tax and unpaid association dues can be paid off at closing. Get a payoff from the Clark County Treasurer and a current statement from the association, pass both to the title company and let your proceeds cover them. A mortgage or recorded lien works the same way.

Association paperwork can drag, so ask early. Buyers like to read the governing documents and a list of assessments before committing.

sections.h2: From offer to closing in Henderson
sections.html:
The order of events is simple. A buyer reviews the house and makes an offer, a title search confirms ownership and flags liens, and you sign the contract together with the disclosure. Closing takes place at a title or escrow office, and the deed and declaration of value then go to the Clark County Recorder.

The items that most often add time in a Henderson sale are association paperwork, a short-term rental registration that needs sorting out, and an estate that has not finished probate. Raise whichever applies on your first call, and the buyer can plan around it.

sections.h2: Preparing a Henderson house for a quick sale
sections.html:
Speed comes from preparation. Before anyone makes an offer, find your deed, the most recent tax bill and any mortgage statement. If the house has an association, order the dues statement and the governing documents at the same time, because those requests move at the association's pace and not yours. Write down what you know about the roof, the cooling system, plumbing and any past water damage. If the house was ever rented to visitors, locate the registration paperwork too.

With that folder in hand, the title company can order its search at once, and a buyer sees a seller who is organized. Sellers who skip this step usually lose days to document requests, not to the buyer.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Henderson
sections.html:
A cash buyer brings no mortgage, which removes the wait for a lender appraisal. Your side is unchanged: hand over the disclosure, deliver clear title, square up any HOA balance, pay a mortgage or lien at closing and sign the deed.

Cash Home Buyers looks at the house in its current state and quotes no number beforehand. An offer you decide against costs you nothing.

  • Gather the deed, a loan payoff statement and your newest tax bill.
  • Ask for an up-to-date HOA statement and governing documents.
  • Note known repairs so the disclosure is complete.

faqs.q: How far is Henderson from Las Vegas?
faqs.a: Roughly 16 miles to the southeast. Both cities sit in Clark County and share a school district.

faqs.q: How much does a Henderson short-term rental registration cost?
faqs.a: $848 per property each year, and it cannot be refunded. On top of that, owners need a Nevada business license, a certification class and a qualifying local contact.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax when I sell in Henderson?
faqs.a: Yes, $2.55 per $500 of value in Clark County. Either side can be charged under NRS 375, so your contract settles who pays.

faqs.q: Do I need to remove my front lawn before selling?
faqs.a: No. The water authority confirms that the turf law leaves single-family grass, front and back, alone.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Henderson property tax assessment?
faqs.a: By January 15, with the County Board of Equalization. A weekend or holiday on that date moves the deadline to the next business day.
